title: Finite Q3 local Gibbs and energy-weighted commutator-sum replacement audit
question: Can the raw finite-Q3 commutator-sum coefficient be replaced, on a named local common-core proxy, by two-sided Gibbs and energy-weighted pair seminorms that remain controlled across the declared cutoff, beta, volume, and shifted source supports?
method: Follow the hash-pinned EXP-001163 Q3 fixture and rebuild every truncated oscillator, onsite term and bond term on volumes 2, 4 and 6 for cutoffs 3, 4, 5 and 6.

For every overlapping term pair compute X=[H_j,H_k] on its union support U; construct the induced local Hamiltonian H_U, normalized local Gibbs matrix rho_U at beta in {1/2,1,2}, and shifted positive K_U.
Evaluate the raw operator norm, two-sided Gibbs Hilbert-Schmidt seminorm, and four-leg K_U^(1/2)-Gibbs seminorm for each pair, then aggregate all pairs and the explicit source-touching support sets.

Check one full tensor embedding per volume for support locality, independently reconstruct the matrix calculation, compare every aggregate row, and compile Lean R334 for exact rational bookkeeping and scope flags.
finding: Primary 247/247 and independent 130/130 assertions pass over 36 volume/cutoff/beta rows; the integrated verifier passes 1129/1129 and Lean R334 compiles. The raw, Gibbs and K^(1/2)-Gibbs sums are finite and agree between lanes within the declared tolerance. The energy-weighted all-pair sum per site grows from cutoff 3 to 6 by ratios 7.8113148179745755 at beta=1/2, 4.35073144591442 at beta=1, and 2.127796987484661 at beta=2, with the same values across the three finite volumes because the induced graph sums are additive on this fixture. The largest weighted per-site value is 31.952418989196214. Source-touching aggregates are finite but boundary-dependent; for example at beta=1, cutoff 6 they are 8.315925195821489 for V=2 source {0,1}, 24.94777558746448 for V=4 source {0,1}, 33.263700783285955 for V=4 source {1,2}, and 33.263700783285955 for each listed V=6 source support. These finite trends do not establish a cutoff-, volume- or beta-uniform coefficient.
decision_reason: The finite local-state proxy is reproducible and lane-independent, so it is retained as the next QFT-facing diagnostic after the raw-norm cutoff boundary. The observed cutoff growth means this particular K_U^(1/2)-Gibbs pair sum cannot be promoted as an unqualified uniform replacement. More importantly, rho_U is only an induced local Gibbs matrix: a global-state transfer, common unbounded core, and cancellation-aware D/delta-D estimate are still required before a common-alpha argument.
boundary: Finite oscillator matrices with the inherited Q3 parameters, volumes 2, 4 and 6, cutoffs 3 through 6, beta in {1/2,1,2}, induced union Hamiltonians and the listed source supports. No global KMS restriction, common operator domain, thermodynamic history, exhaustion independence, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or Clay conclusion follows.
next_action: Use the finite growth as a route-local boundary and attempt a global-state-compatible cancellation-aware D,delta-D estimate on the analytic matching-layer common core; if no uniform estimate survives, record the obstruction before any common-alpha promotion.
open: global Gibbs/KMS state transfer for local seminorms
cutoff-, volume- and beta-uniform weighted commutator coefficient
common unbounded operator domain and core density
source/beta/volume-uniform direct D and delta-D Cauchy
gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A

adversarial_review.check: The normalized rho_U is explicitly induced by H_U and is never treated as an infinite-volume KMS restriction or product state.
All four K^(1/2)-Gibbs legs are evaluated separately, so no commutation of K_U, rho_U and X is assumed.
Disjoint pairs are excluded by tensor support and one full embedding per volume agrees with the union-support norm within tolerance.
Every row rebuilds oscillator, H_U, rho_U and K_U for its own cutoff and beta; finite ratios are not asymptotic statements.
Only the explicitly declared source supports are aggregated, and boundary-dependent counts are retained rather than generalized.
Weighted sums are candidate diagnostics; no raw operator-norm Lie-Trotter inequality is silently reused for a seminorm without a proved defect estimate.
R334 checks exact rational fixtures only; spectral matrix calculations and all domain/limit claims remain Python/open analysis.
Common core, thermodynamic dynamics, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.

qft_interface.closed: Finite local-union raw, Gibbs and K^(1/2)-Gibbs commutator-sum tables with independent and Lean cross-checks.
qft_interface.open: Global-state transfer, a cutoff/volume/beta-uniform weighted coefficient, common domain, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, thermodynamic history, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference or Sector-A closure is supplied.

no_overclaim: This finite local-state proxy audit does not prove a global KMS state, common unbounded core, thermodynamic QFT dynamics, a mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
